items.title: David Torkanowsky interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019
items.q: Interviewee discusses Steve Cropper's solo on a record he loves, but does not mention meeting or working with him.

ctx.x: I mean it’s classic. I fucking love that record. I love it.

The reason I thought of it is because you said it just has to sound real. And I’m so fascinated by that record because like first of all it’s just got that sound, but when Steve Cropper comes in on his solo it’s like really too loud and then it gets too soft, and then it gets just right. And I was thinking man, if they had said, “Look the balance is off, do it again, do it five more times.”

I love people that make records and leave mistakes on their records. I love that. It’s just like come on — it’s a snapshot in time, and it’s again, where intent trumps execution. I try not to work in the studio with any engineer that doesn’t know what this is [gestures]. “Where’s the guitar solo, where’s the guitar solo, oh it’s around my neck.” You know? I mean we can all perform meticulously perfect sonic surgery with ProTools and I’ve used ProTools as well. But, ‘cause it’s a studio standard and it’s great,…
